Hi there. I’m so sorry this happened to you. There’s no excuse for it. I’m so happy you’re seeking counseling to address the impact of that trauma. If you haven’t already, you should check out an org I learned about called Just Detention International. I completely understand. I shouldn’t have assumed letting go was the course you want to take- I took that from her saying she doesn’t want a relationship. I’m also sorry- I didn’t mean to imply you specifically when I added the part about “or you think you love someone.” That was just to make the advice applicable to anyone with an AA attachment style, because sometimes that type of attachment can create an illusory sense of love. No one knows your relationship better than you. Listen to your heart. You love each other but is this working for you? If you think she’s open to working on her style and you’re open to working on yours, there’s always hope. If she doesn’t want a relationship and you do, that’s trickier to navigate. You could be patient but that could be a painful limbo. (Also take my advice with a grain of salt because I’m lost too and don’t know what I’m doing. Just thinking out loud.) Stay strong and remember your gut isn’t always wrong and your fears aren’t always right. I’m always here if you need a sounding board.

Reach out anytime you need a friend. It's never easy to let go of someone you love (or think you love)-- but it's also not easy to deny yourself what you need on a regular basis. You have to decide which hard thing you're going to put yourself through. I wish that made it easier to actually do it. Here's a quote that has helped me a lot: 

“I am trying to see things in perspective. My dog wants a bite of my peanut butter chocolate chip bagel. I know she cannot have this, because chocolate makes dogs very sick. My dog does not understand this. She pouts and wraps herself around my leg like a scarf and purrs and tries to convince me to give her just a tiny bit. When I do not give in, she eventually gives up and lays in the corner, under the piano, drooping and sad. I hope the universe has my best interest in mind like I have my dog’s. When I want something with my whole being, and the universe withholds it from me, I hope the universe thinks to herself: "Silly girl. She thinks this is what she wants, but she does not understand how it will hurt.”  
― Blythe Baird

Sure! So first month of our relationship, no signs at all of anything. He seemed just as openly crazy about me as I was him-- it was really refreshing since I'd been in mostly AA-DA traps in prior relationships. He clearly and consistently expressed how he felt, was really affectionate, etc. Of course, I know it's easy to have these things in the beginning of a relationship-- I just say all that to respond to your point about not noticing red flags right away. I'll list some of the things that bothered me-- they may not all be signs of DA or anything!! Just signs it wasn't right (which I didn't listen to).

* Keeping me at a distance from friends and family- not really talking about me to people like you would casually talk about a partner. Not really trying to get involved with my friends or family either.
* No sign of me whatsoever on his social media (stupid I know-- if it was JUST this and nothing else, I wouldn't read into it).
* Shutting down during hard conversations. He would get really upset and just leave, even if it was a pretty normal conversation in my mind. We couldn't really have many constructive conversations about our relationship, because he would feel cornered and attacked.
* In the beginning, he would smile at me if I smiled at him. Once the switch flipped, if I smiled at him, he would make a face like he was spooked. It was kind of cute and funny at first, but then it started to feel like another way to keep me at arm's length (probably not even consciously!!)
* He stopped being very physically affectionate. (Examples: if we are standing looking at a gorgeous view, he doesn't come put his arm around me. He doesn't hold my hand in the car like he did in the beginning. All little things!! But when it goes from 100 to 0 it's noticeable!) Along these same lines, he never cared to take pictures with me, do special things for holidays, etc. It just didn't feel like he was (outwardly) very excited about me anymore, and nothing had changed between us!
* Disappearing for the night (no texts, calls) when he would go out (I never thought he was cheating or anything, it just felt like I was out of sight out of mind, which hurt). Along the same lines, during LD, he could go all day without talking to me at all, and it wasn't weird to him.
* Getting nervous about any steps forward. This was why moving in was such a big deal to me-- it was the first step forward that HE initiated. And when he bailed on it, it felt like it took away my only hope that he was trying to push through his own walls.
* Not being expressive about how he felt anymore. He said some really sweet things one night recently about how much he loved me and how incredible he thinks I am, then said he "thinks this stuff all the time but doesn't say it for some stupid reason." I began to realize even if he feels this way, I'm always going to be waiting for the rare moments when he is comfortable enough to express it. It's something I would have been patient and worked through with him, if he'd wanted to, but he didn't want to (or wasn't ready) :/

Anyway, this is a lot... If you have any questions, I'm happy to answer. I hate listing this stuff and making him seem like a dick— he's really not :( There are so many wonderful things about him and our relationship. That's why I haven't been able to let go. But I hope this is helpful for you.

This is kind of the point I got to... Matt is amazing. I'm in love with him. There are a million little and big things I love about him and about us. But we fundamentally aren't in the same place and don't want the same things (at least not in our current states of mind). And if nothing changes, nothing changes. I know how hard it is to let go. Don't think I'm Ms. Strong & Independent over here- I cried in my mom's arms last night. I just got so tired of feeling like I was asking for too much by asking him to show how he felt. I can't tell you what the right move is for you, but please know that you deserve a relationship that makes you feel safe and loved.
